landmarks.summary: All nine names were found in at least one source with a Montana count. Six have two or more sources: Loyola Sacred Heart High School (NCES private 2023-24 and HIFLD private copy), Hellgate High School (NCES public 2024-25 and HIFLD public copy), Rose Park (TIGER K2180 and PAD-US 'Rose Garden' at the same place), Missoula Montana Airport (FAA NASR 2026-10-01 'MISSOULA MONTANA', HIFLD aviation copy, TIGER 'Missoula International'), Community Medical Center and St Patrick Hospital (each in the HIFLD hospitals copy, FAA heliport records and TIGER K1231). Three rest on one source each: Sacajawea Park and McCormick Park (PAD-US 4.1 Fee, City of Missoula local parks) and St. Paul Lutheran church (FEMA copy of the IRS-based places-of-worship layer). Montana counts: NCES public 854 (2024-25) and private 109 (2023-24); HIFLD copies public 837, private 102, hospitals 71, aviation 320; FAA APT 318; places of worship 1074; PAD-US Fee 1457; TIGER K2180 104, K2184 101, K2188 22 (917 area landmarks in all); USGS fire and EMS 461. Licence: NCES text says public domain; PAD-US text says public domain; TIGER says free to use with acknowledgement; the HIFLD NTAD aviation copy quotes the US government work statement. Not verified: the HIFLD public school and hospital copies have no licence text; the places-of-worship points come from a commercial geocoder whose terms were not checked; the DPHHS licensure terms were not found. The evidence log is plain text (notes.txt), not notes.md, because the agent rules bar report-style .md files. Downloads total 25437209 bytes, far under the 600 MB limit; no git writes; nothing written under /home/user/wt.
blockers: maps.bts.dot.gov (the NTAD airports MapServer) returned 502 (CONNECT tunnel failed). The FAA NASR APT file was used instead.
nfdc.faa.gov returned 503 from the origin for the 2026-10-01 zip names other than APT.zip (which returned 200). Only APT.zip was used.

The HIFLD copies used (public schools, private schools, hospitals, aviation) sit under the account tqd32886_USG, not confirmed as an official HIFLD Open organisation. The HIFLD hub dataset list was not parsed, so provenance and currency are not confirmed.
No HIFLD-owned national fire station layer was found in the searches. The USGS National Map Structures layer 51 was used as a substitute.

Terms not verified: the commercial geocoder behind the places-of-worship points; the Montana DPHHS licensure data behind the hospital copy; the FAA APT file itself; the usgs.gov PAD-US and TNM terms pages (www.usgs.gov was not read); the HIFLD public school and hospital copies (no licence text found).
The PAD-US 4.1 Montana file via ScienceBase (109752792 bytes, from the earlier brief) was not retried in this session. The PAD-US ArcGIS Fee layer was used instead.
The DPHHS source link in the HIFLD hospitals copy has moved (301 to https://dphhs.mt.gov/oig/Licensure/), so the credited URL is stale.

verdicts.layer: NCES EDGE public school geocodes (CCD), layer 'Public School Locations 2024-25'
verdicts.claim: Montana has 854 public school points in the NCES EDGE 2024-25 layer. Hellgate High School is listed at 925 Gerald Ave, Missoula 59801 (NCESSCH 301854000562; lat 46.86272, lon -113.99634).

verdicts.reason: Stands with a note. The 854 count holds on every check I ran. STFIP '30' returns 854, all 854 of those points fall inside the Montana boundary, and a bounding-box pull of 961 schools finds the same 854 inside Montana. The licence sentence, the Hellgate High School record, the Missoula county count (47), the four other Hellgate names, the absence of church rows and the attribute size (210,849 bytes for an 11-field pull, claim 208,233) all match. The note: the STATE text field 'MT' returns 857, not 854, because three records with Montana addresses and ZIP codes are coded to North Dakota (STFIP 38) and lie outside Montana. Counts should use STFIP or geometry, not the STATE text, and the claim should say which field it used.
verdicts.evidence:
1. Layer metadata, https://nces.ed.gov/opengis/rest/services/K12_School_Locations/EDGE_GEOCODE_PUBLICSCH_2425/MapServer/0?f=json (read with python -I). Name "Public School Locations 2024-25"; copyrightText "NCES EDGE"; geometryType esriGeometryPoint. Description ends: "All information contained in this file is in the public domain. Data users are advised to review NCES program documentation and feature class metadata to understand the limitations and appropriate use of these data." It also says the layer "develops annually updated point locations (latitude and longitude) for public elementary and secondary schools included in the NCES Common Core of Data (CCD)" and was "developed from the 2024-2025 CCD collection". Field notes: STFIP = "State FIPS"; STATE = "Reported location state"; OPSTFIPS = "FIPS state code for operating state".

2. Counts, query endpoint .../MapServer/0/query with returnCountOnly: STFIP='30' 854; where 1=1 102178; STATE='MT' 857; OPSTFIPS='30' 852; STFIP='30' AND CNTY='30063' 47; STFIP='30' AND CITY='Missoula' 26; city or county union 47. returnIdsOnly for STFIP='30' gives 854 IDs, all unique.

3. Hellgate High School, NCESSCH 301854000562: NAME "Hellgate High School", STREET "925 Gerald Ave", CITY "Missoula", ZIP "59801", LAT 46.86272, LON -113.996336, LEAID 3018540, CNTY 30063 "Missoula County". Bytes for Montana: 11-field attribute pull (NCESSCH, LEAID, NAME, STREET, CITY, STATE, ZIP, STFIP, NMCNTY, LAT, LON; no geometry), 854 features, 210,849 bytes (claim 208,233; difference 1.3 percent). All-field attribute pull, 854 features, 380,416 bytes. STFIP 30 with geometry (10 fields), 235,028 bytes. Bounding-box pull (961 schools) with geometry, 264,718 bytes.

Geometry check against the Montana boundary from https://tigerweb.geo.census.gov/arcgis/rest/services/TIGERweb/State_County/MapServer/0 (STATE='30', maxAllowableOffset 0.0005 degrees; one ring, 2,522 vertices). Bounding box: 854 of 961 schools inside Montana, all with STFIP 30 and STATE 'MT'; 107 outside.

Three STATE='MT' records not coded 30, all outside the Montana line. 380567000826 SQUAW GAP SCHOOL (494 Hwy 16 N, Sidney, MT 59270; STFIP 38; CNTY 38053 McKenzie County; LAT 47.488081, LON -103.925887; 9.09 km outside; Census address match returned no result). 382034000714 EAST FAIRVIEW ELEMENTARY SCHOOL and 382034000951 YELLOWSTONE VIRTUAL ACADEMY (both 301 2nd St S, Fairview, MT 59221; STFIP 38; LAT 47.85589, LON -104.038071; 0.26 km outside). Census matched "301 2ND ST, FAIRVIEW, MT, 59221" at x -104.046170, y 47.855371, inside Montana, so the NCES point is probably the error for the Fairview pair.

8. Two STFIP-30 records with OPSTFIPS 59 instead of 30: 590004100002 Northern Cheyenne Tribal School (Busby) and 590017800129 Two Eagle River School (Pablo). Both lie inside Montana, so they are part of the 854. I did not confirm what code 59 means in an NCES code list.

The service folder, https://nces.ed.gov/opengis/rest/services/K12_School_Locations?f=json, lists EDGE_GEOCODE_PUBLICSCH layers for 1516, 1617, 1718, 1819, 1920, 2021, 2122, 2223, 2324 and 2425. Small API responses went straight into that folder rather than one folder each; the only file download was the 186 KB Census cartographic state zip (state_cb_zip/), which I listed but did not use, because its 1:20 million generalization is coarser than the 0.26 km margin. Other files in the same folder (count_all.json, count_mt.json, count_mt_opstfips.json, hellgate_names_all.json, and later cnt_*.json, mt_attrs_*.json, osm_hellgate.json, page_schoollocations.html) were not written by me and I did not read them. Refuted on the size evidence. The core record stands: PAD-US Fee OBJECTID 118981 is 'Sacajawea', Des_Tp 'LP', Loc_Own 'City of Missoula', GIS_Acres 2. The vertex-mean centroid reproduces exactly (lat 46.86351, lon -114.00281). The Montana count is 1457 polygons. The public-domain sentence is quoted correctly. TIGER and GNIS have no Missoula Sacajawea entry. The distance is about 1.2 km (1,208 m) to the Missoula County Courthouse.

Two size statements are wrong. (1) The '16 acres in the Public Access layer' is not Missoula's size. PADUS_Public_Access OBJECTID 224213 ('Sacajawea', GIS_Acres 16) is one feature with two rings: a Missoula ring of 1.63 acres and a Sioux City, Iowa ring of 14.27 acres, which is the same polygon as Fee OBJECTID 201629 (GIS_Acres 14). The 16 is 2 + 14. The Missoula park is about 1.6 acres in that layer, roughly a tenth of the claimed size. (2) The 133,172-byte figure fits only a narrow field set (three fields = 140,574 bytes). The full attribute table without geometry is 1,326,081 bytes as JSON, about ten times the claim, so the size is off by more than a factor of two under the usual reading of 'attribute-only'.

verdicts.reason: Refuted on the Public Access acreage and the byte size. The core identification stands. (1) "16 acres in the Public Access layer" is not this park's area. The 16-acre record named "Sacajawea" (PADUS_Public_Access OBJECTID 224213, GIS_Acres 16) is a merged feature. Its Missoula ring is 1.63 acres. Its other ring, 14.28 acres at about 42.47 N, -96.38 W, is the Sioux City, Iowa "Sacajawea" (Fee OBJECTID 201629, GIS_Acres 14; 42 of 43 distinct vertices shared). The Missoula park is about 1.6 acres in that layer, roughly a tenfold error. (2) The 133,172-byte "attribute-only" figure matches only a three-field JSON (140,600 bytes). All 37 attribute fields as JSON are 1,326,081 bytes, about ten times the claim. Stands with notes: the Fee record (OBJECTID 118981, Unit_Nm "Sacajawea", Loc_Own "City of Missoula", Des_Tp LP, Pub_Access OA, GIS_Acres 2) and the centroid 46.86351, -114.00281 reproduce exactly; the Montana count of 1,457 matches; the public-domain sentence is quoted verbatim (the "terms of use" sentence is paraphrased loosely); TIGER 2026 and GNIS have no Missoula entry. "Exists in one source" needs a note: OpenStreetMap (ODbL, not public domain) also has Sacajawea Park in Missoula. "PAD-US writes the name without the word Park" holds only for this record: the same Montana Fee layer names the Billings, Bozeman and Polson parks "Sacajawea Park". "About 1.2 km from downtown" holds for the Missoula County Courthouse (1.21 km) but not for every downtown point (0.93 km to the OSM city point, 2.15 km to the TIGER city point).

PAD-US 4.1 has no 'Rose Park', but it has 'Rose Garden' (City of Missoula, Local Park, 4 acres) whose polygon centroid is about 4 m from the TIGER point, so it is very likely the same park under another name (an inference from coordinates).

verdicts.reason:
Refuted on two points. The coordinate match itself stands.

(1) Size. The claim gives 133172 bytes for the Montana Fee layer, attributes only. The same query (State_Nm = 'MT', returnGeometry false, all fields) returns 1326081 bytes for 1457 features and 37 fields, about ten times the claimed figure. The claimed number only matches a narrow field subset: Unit_Nm alone gives 81443 bytes, and five chosen fields give 196238 to 213407 bytes. The claim names no field list, so as worded the size is off by more than a factor of two.

(2) Fact. "PAD-US 4.1 has no Rose Park" is false as worded. The Montana Fee layer has two features named Rose Park: OBJECTID 98589 (City of Bozeman, Local Park, 21 acres) and OBJECTID 154664 (County of Yellowstone, Local Park, 25 acres). The Missoula-only version is true: none of the 13 fee features within about 2 km of the TIGER point is named Rose Park.

Stands: K2180 is defined as Park in the TIGER feature catalogue. The TIGER interior point is in Missoula County (GEOID 30063, confirmed by two services). Rose Garden is City of Missoula, Local Park (code LP in the layer domain), 3.76 acres by polygon area. The TIGER zip is 444672 bytes. Both licence quotes are accurate.

Notes (wording, not refutations): the true area centroid is 5.5 m from the TIGER point, not about 4 m. The 3.2 m figure needs the closing ring vertex counted twice, and that version reproduces the claimed vertex mean to 0.4 m. The garden polygon lies wholly inside the TIGER Rose Park polygon, so "same park" is a containment inference, not an identity. The 1.9 km figure matches the Missoula County Courthouse (1916 m), which the claim does not name. The usgs.gov terms link returned HTTP 403 on one try.

verdicts.reason: Refuted on one stated figure: the PAD-US Montana attribute size. The rest stands, with notes. The claim gives 133172 bytes attribute-only for the Montana Fee layer. Stored as a file, the same 1457 features with 37 attribute fields are 1326081 bytes as JSON, 1356871 as GeoJSON and 545924 as CSV, which is about 4 to 16 times the claim. The claim matches only a gzip transfer (72950 to 89417 bytes, so the claim is 1.5 to 1.8 times the transfer size) or a reduced field list, and the claim names neither. The TIGER zip size is exact (444672 bytes), and the stated licences are as written. Notes that do not refute: (1) Rose Park exists in TIGER 2026 as K2180 Park, with interior point +46.8567358, -114.0052328, 0.5 m from the claimed point, and it lies in Missoula County (GEOID 30063). (2) PAD-US Rose Garden is City of Missoula, Des_Tp LP (layer domain: Local Park), 4 acres (3.76 acres from the polygon). (3) The 3.7 m distance reproduces only when the closing vertex of the ring is counted twice. The true area centroid is 5.5 m from the TIGER point, and the vertex mean without the duplicate is 8.1 m; all are under 10 m. (4) PAD-US has no Rose Park in Missoula, but Montana does have Rose Park records in Bozeman (21 acres) and Yellowstone County (25 acres), so the claim should say Missoula. (5) No downtown point is named, so 1.9 km could not be matched; the TIGER Missoula city interior point is 2.5 km away. (6) The whole PAD-US Rose Garden polygon lies inside the larger TIGER Rose Park polygon (6.22 vs 3.76 acres). The city's Memorial Rose Garden Park at 800 Brooks St geocodes 61 m from the TIGER point, inside its polygon, so 'same park under another name' is better stated as 'the garden lies inside the Rose Park area'. (7) PAD-US is described as public domain with attribution requested, and no official City of Missoula page naming Rose Park was found.

verdicts.reason: Refuted on the one-source conclusion. The claim says TIGER has no Missoula McCormick park. That is wrong for TIGER point landmarks. The TIGER 2026 point file (tl_2026_30_pointlm.zip) lists "Mc Cormick Park", MTFCC K2190 (a park class), at lat 46.8729580, lon -114.0038840. The TIGER 2025 point file lists the same point. That point lies inside the PAD-US polygon "Mccormick Park" (OBJECTID 118963), so the park appears in at least two sources, not one. The TIGER areal landmark file (AREALM 2026) has no match, so the claim holds only for areal landmarks. Everything else stands: the two PAD-US Missoula rows (26 and 1 acres, City of Missoula, LP), the vertex-mean centroid 46.87141, -114.00392, the 1,457 Montana polygons, the "Public Domain" rights text, the GNIS Flat row in Beaverhead County, the exact 1,518,121-byte GNIS zip, and the distance of about 0.8 km (0.76 km from the GNIS Missoula populated place point; the claim does not define downtown).

verdicts.reason: Refuted, because two statements in the claim are false, although the PAD-US row itself checks out. First, TIGER does have this park: the point 'Mc Cormick Park' (MTFCC K2190, a park code) sits at lat 46.872958, lon -114.003884, inside both the PAD-US 'Mccormick Park' polygon and the City of Missoula 'McCormick' polygon, and the Census geocoder places it in Missoula city. Second, the park is not in one source only: the City of Missoula Parkland_mso layer also lists 'McCormick' and 'Little McCormick' in Missoula, so 'exists in one source' is wrong. What stands: the Montana Fee layer has 1,457 rows; 'Mccormick Park' is Local Park (LP), City of Missoula, GIS_Acres 26 (my measured area 25.65 acres); 'Little Mccormick Park' is 1 acre; the public-domain wording is quoted accurately; GNIS has McCormick Park (Flat, Beaverhead County) and no Missoula park of that name; and the 133,172-byte figure reproduces exactly for a three-field JSON response (Unit_Nm, Des_Tp, Own_Type).

verdicts.claim: St. Paul Lutheran church exists in one source: ST PAUL LUTHERAN CHURCH OF MISSOULA at 202 BROOKS ST, Missoula 59801 (X -113.999002, Y 46.861895; POINTADDRESS, score 100), about 1.2 km from downtown. The point was geocoded by a commercial geocoder whose terms were not checked.

verdicts.reason: Stands with a note. I found no wrong fact, no misread licence, no count or size off by more than a factor of two, and the source was reachable on the first try. Layer 42 holds the record as claimed: ST PAUL LUTHERAN CHURCH OF MISSOULA, 202 BROOKS ST, MISSOULA, ZIP 59801, X -113.999002, Y 46.861895, LOC_NAME POINTADDRESS, SCORE 100. Montana has 1074 rows and Missoula has 82. The licence sentence is quoted exactly. A public address geocode puts 202 Brooks St about 40 m from the point, and an IRS-derived record for the same EIN lists the same street address. Notes: (1) The point carries the provenance of a named commercial geocoder, and I could not read that provider's current terms because both of its pages failed (404 and 503). The owner's "no use limitations" line covers the dataset, not that geocoder's terms, so check those terms before publishing these coordinates. (2) There is no update schedule. The copy was downloaded July 22, 2024, and maintenance code 012 means unknown. (3) The 293018-byte figure has no stated format. It is within 10 percent of a seven-field GeoJSON export of the 1074 rows (274,422 bytes), so it is within a factor of two. (4) "About 1.2 km from downtown" holds for two of three downtown reference addresses (1.20 and 1.22 km), and the third is 0.96 km away. "Downtown" is not defined. (5) "Exists in one source" is true only of the layer. An IRS-derived record and a church directory also list the church, and I could not confirm that the congregation is active today.

verdicts.reason: Refuted for the all-attributes size only. The name-only figures stand. A fresh pull of layer 4 (Flowline - Small Scale) over a separate Montana outline gave 55,579 named flowlines (claim 55,586), 1,900,251 vertices (claim 1,900,461), 47,353,942 name-only bytes (claim 47,359,254) and 10,850,765 gzip bytes (claim 10,851,976). Each is within 0.02 percent, using the claim's method (compact JSON, UTF-8, 5-decimal rounding, whole FeatureCollection). The claim's "52,746,996 bytes with all attributes" is wrong. Layer 4 has 133 schema fields and 132 come back per feature; the same method gives 165,336,460 bytes, 3.13 times the claim. The claim's figure matches a short field list: the team's test query asked for COMID, GNIS_NAME, LENGTHKM, FTYPE and FCODE, and those five fields give 51,518,280 bytes here. Their saved manifests show about 848 bytes of server output per feature, which fits a short list, not 132 fields. Two notes that do not refute: the source is the small-scale layer (layer 4), while the high-resolution layer 6 (Flowline - Large Scale) has 193,008 named features touching Montana, 3.47 times layer 4, and was not measured; and the licence "As B2" could not be checked because B2's text was not found in the landmark folders. The NHD metadata says access and use constraints are "None", with acknowledgment of USGS requested.
